# M8 static reconstruction fixtures

The following are unchanged CC0 inputs from the official JPEG XL conformance corpus,
revision `4bf053529c7cefd2951be453475bb3dccc7e7be8`.

| File | Official case | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| noise.jxl | noise | 20cddadc3fdbae331a912dba0d14e6326008094d7a16d006961ccdeac2bc9950 |
| opsin-inverse.jxl | opsin_inverse | 5c25ba126e6fb3536a12ca191b92f1c3be86ee74683688ed56c94804db5d2e16 |

`benchmark/jpegxl/production-program/m8-static-native.json` records independent
native sRGB comparisons and the first-party output hashes. The float-domain
sequence verification also checks these inputs without an 8-bit quantization
step.

The following interaction fixtures supplement the official inputs:

- `custom-upsampling.jxl` derives from the CC0 `upsampling` case. Its image
  header supplies 55 binary16 weights of 0.04 for factor-four reconstruction.
  The original frame payload is unchanged.
- `custom-filters-lossless.jxl` and `custom-filters-lossy.jxl` use repository
  generated RGB patterns with custom Gaborish, sharpness, channel weights and
  sigma settings. Regenerate with
  `node benchmark/jpegxl/generate-m8-custom-filters.ts`.
- `weighted-patches.jxl` uses two repository generated RGBA frames. Eight
  rectangles exercise all patch blend modes, including below/above alpha blends,
  alpha-weighted addition and a reference saved before color transformation.
  Regenerate with `node benchmark/jpegxl/generate-m8-weighted-patches.ts`.
  `weighted-patches.reference.f32` contains the pinned native decoder's two
  composited frames as little-endian interleaved RGBA float32 samples. It is
  the payload of its NPY output, without the NPY header.

Repository generated patterns and their encoded/reference pixels are licensed
under the repository MIT license. Native decoder version, binary hash, fixture
hashes and per-channel comparison results are recorded by the M8 verifiers.

`patches.jxl` and `progressive.jxl` are unchanged CC0 official cases from the
same revision. They test native layer dependency reconstruction against pinned
native NPY output. `m8-native-raw.json` records that comparison.

`weighted-patches-lossy.jxl` applies the same eight patch modes to M7 XYB color
with exact alpha. Its `.reference.f32` file is the native NPY float payload.
The weighted-patches generator produces both lossless and lossy variants.

`modular-ycbcr-{444,422,420,noise,splines}.jxl` use repository generated signed
Cb/Y/Cr planes. The last two combine YCbCr with synthetic noise or a spline.
Regenerate with `node benchmark/jpegxl/generate-m8-ycbcr.ts`. Every output is
compared to native sRGB, with maximum error one 8-bit code value.

`noise-upsampling.jxl` combines photon noise with factor-two reconstruction.
The repository generated input is `noise-upsampling.source.png`. Reproduce with
the pinned `cjxl` and arguments `-d 2 -e 3 --resampling=2
--photon_noise_iso=3200 --num_threads=1`. Its input hash and native comparison
are recorded in `m8-static-native.json`.

`wide-gamut.jxl` is one lossy Display P3 animation frame generated by
`node benchmark/jpegxl/generate-m8-wide-gamut.ts`. Pinned native sRGB float
output verifies the pixels. The sequence regression also verifies that its
emitted sRGB values are not labeled with a linear transfer; the original Display
P3 descriptor remains in the header.
